title: The Impetus Thermometer
opening: A single difficult session can take over your memory of a whole pursuit. This practice keeps each report beside its situation so you can notice whether the relationship changes over time.

labels.exampleNote: Illustrative pattern only. The manuscript supplies no readings for this example.
labels.figure: Hypothetical reports from one person on that person's own scale: perceived value stays similar while perceived difficulty rises over three intervals. Late-night sessions are context to investigate, not a proven cause.
labels.exampleReading: The reports point to a question about the late sessions. They do not prove why difficulty rose, show that the project lost value, or decide whether to continue.
labels.separateEvent: A serious or urgent event still needs attention when it happens. Do not average it away or wait for a trend.
labels.practiceIntro: Choose an interval that fits the pursuit. Use the same personal scale each time, then record the situation and any trigger beside both ratings. Add another interval when it occurs; compare the reports without calculating a total.
labels.scaleNote: For this private record, the controls use 1 to 10. Choose what the low and high ends mean for you and keep those meanings. These are subjective reports, not objective units, a clinical measure, or a comparison between people.
labels.lowAnchor: What does a low rating mean to you?
labels.highAnchor: What does a high rating mean to you?
labels.interval: When was this reading? Use a date or a clear interval name.
labels.value: Perceived value, on your scale (1 to 10)
labels.difficulty: Perceived difficulty, on your scale (1 to 10)
labels.situation: What was the situation around both ratings?
labels.trigger: What changed or may have triggered the reading? Leave this uncertain if you do not know.
labels.private: This record is private to your lesson practice. It is optional; saving is separate from entering a draft.
labels.trend: When difficulty approaches or passes value, inspect the cause with the Difficulty Diagnostic or Passion Balancer. The ratings cue an investigation; they do not make the decision for you.
labels.sourceQuote: At consistent intervals, rate perceived value and difficulty on the same scale. Record the situation and triggers beside both ratings. Look for a trend. When difficulty approaches or exceeds value, use the Difficulty Diagnostic or Passion Balancer to locate the cause and choose a response.

labels.sourceBoundary: The source gives no objective unit, clinical threshold, or universal interval. Examples and application guidance here are authored for this expansion; they are not observed learner results.
